title: The guestbook
style: cinematic horror film still, dramatic moody lighting, lonely 1970s roadside motel at night in the rain, buzzing pink neon and sodium orange glow against deep blue darkness, wood paneling and worn carpet, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, subject clearly visible, no text, no watermark
caption:
Part 2. Nobody who signed for Room 9 ever signed out. 📖

Original fiction. Part 3 tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Last time: Marcus rented Room 9 against the only rule, and the guestbook signed itself with tomorrow's date.
scenes.image: an old leather guestbook open on a motel counter at night, a pen lying across the page, neon glow through the window

scenes.narration: In the morning, Room 9 was made up. Bed tight. Towels folded. No raincoat. No guest. The key was back on its hook.
scenes.image: perfectly made motel bed in an empty room, grey morning light through thin orange curtains

scenes.narration: Mr. Dell didn't yell. He just went grey in the face and said: then you'd better read it. All of it.
scenes.image: older man in a cardigan sitting heavily in a motel office chair, face in shadow, rain on the window

scenes.narration: The guestbook went back to 1964. Thousands of guests. Marcus started flipping, and he saw the pattern on the very first page.
scenes.image: thick old leather guestbook with yellowed pages on a desk, dust floating in lamplight

scenes.narration: Every guest has a check-in line and a checkout line. Except the ones who stayed in Room 9.
scenes.image: a man's finger tracing down a column of faded ink in an old ledger, illegible handwriting

scenes.narration: Nobody who signed for Room 9 ever signed out. Not in the sixties. Not in the nineties. Not last spring. Dozens of names. One room. All still checked in.
scenes.image: a single motel door at the end of a row at night, faint warm light leaking around its edges

scenes.narration: The first name belonged to a traveling salesman. Reported missing in the fall of 1964. His car was found in this parking lot. Engine still running.
scenes.image: an old 1960s sedan alone in a motel parking lot at dawn, exhaust mist curling from the tailpipe

scenes.narration: Marcus read faster. Room 9. Room 9. Room 9. All the way to the last page.
scenes.image: pages of an old guestbook fanning past in a blur under a desk lamp

scenes.narration: The newest entry was last night's. The one the pen wrote by itself. Under the lamp, he could finally read it.
scenes.image: close-up of a man's face leaning into a desk lamp's circle of light, eyes narrowed at a page

scenes.narration: The handwriting was his. Every loop. Every slant. So was the name. Marcus Hale. Room 9. Check-in: tonight.
scenes.image: a man frozen behind a motel desk, guestbook open in front of him, the neon outside flickering off
